questions.q: Colleague left. No docs. Fastest way in?
questions.explain: PRISM answers in plain English and cites the file and line, so you skip the 200-file hunt.

questions.q: New system landed on your desk. First move?
questions.explain: Start by asking. PRISM gives you the big picture in minutes and shows where each part lives.

questions.q: Boss asks how the code works. You?
questions.explain: PRISM explains what the code does and points to the lines that prove it.

questions.q: The only expert is on leave. Now what?
questions.explain: The knowledge is in the code. PRISM reads it for you, so nobody is a bottleneck.

questions.q: Nobody remembers why this rule exists. Quickest answer?
questions.explain: PRISM finds the rule in the code and explains what it does, with the source to check.

questions.q: Need to understand a system by Friday?
questions.explain: A few clear questions to PRISM get you understanding in minutes, not weeks.

questions.q: Handover notes are two years old. Best check?
questions.explain: PRISM answers from the code as it is now, not from notes that have gone stale.

questions.q: Docs and code disagree. What settles it?
questions.explain: The code is what actually runs. PRISM cites it, so you can settle it by looking.

questions.q: Small change needed. Unsure what it affects?
questions.explain: PRISM shows where a piece of code is used, so you know the impact before you touch it.

questions.q: Which question should you ask PRISM?
questions.explain: A clear, specific question gets a clear, specific answer with a source.

questions.q: Which question gets a useful answer?
questions.explain: Name the thing you want to understand. PRISM does the searching.

questions.q: Which question is clearest?
questions.explain: Asking about one step in plain English lets PRISM walk you through it.

questions.q: You want to understand refunds. Ask PRISM:
questions.explain: Ask how something is done. PRISM explains the steps and cites each one.

questions.q: Best way to ask about a figure?
questions.explain: Ask how the figure is calculated and PRISM traces it back to the code.

questions.q: Which question will PRISM answer best?
questions.explain: One focused question beats one giant one. You can always ask a follow-up.

questions.q: PRISM works best when you ask:
questions.explain: Plain English, one thing at a time. No special syntax needed.

questions.q: Which question is most specific?
questions.explain: The more specific the question, the more precise the answer and its citation.

questions.q: First answer was too broad. Next step?
questions.explain: Follow up like a conversation. PRISM narrows down and cites the exact spot.

questions.q: Which answer can you trust?
questions.explain: An answer that names the file and line can be checked in seconds.

questions.q: Which answer can you check yourself?
questions.explain: A citation turns "trust me" into "see for yourself".

questions.q: Why does PRISM show its sources?
questions.explain: Every PRISM answer points to its source, so you never have to take it on faith.

questions.q: An answer with no source is...
questions.explain: Without a source it may be right, but you cannot tell. PRISM gives you the source.

questions.q: Two answers sound right. Which do you trust?
questions.explain: Confidence is not evidence. A citation is.

questions.q: PRISM cites a file and line. Why useful?
questions.explain: You can open the cited line and confirm the answer yourself.

questions.q: Which reply would satisfy an auditor?
questions.explain: Auditors need evidence. PRISM points to where the rule is written.

questions.q: The answer cites a file. Smart next step?
questions.explain: Citations are there to be used. One look confirms the answer.

questions.q: Which answer is easiest to double-check?
questions.explain: A file and line number is the shortest path to checking an answer.

questions.q: Auditor asks how a figure is calculated. Who helps?
questions.explain: PRISM explains the calculation and cites the code behind it.

questions.q: New hire on day one. What speeds them up?
questions.explain: New joiners ask PRISM in plain English and get up to speed in minutes.

questions.q: Who can use PRISM?
questions.explain: If you can ask a question in plain English, you can use PRISM.

questions.q: Manager needs a quick system summary. Best source?
questions.explain: PRISM summarises what the system does today, in words anyone can follow.

questions.q: Officer asks which rule the code applies?
questions.explain: PRISM shows which rule the code applies and where, so you can confirm it.

questions.q: Team is taking over an old system. They need?
questions.explain: PRISM explains inherited systems so the new team is not starting from zero.

questions.q: Reviewer asks where a rule lives. You show:
questions.explain: PRISM answers "where is this?" with the exact file and line.

questions.q: Who benefits when answers include sources?
questions.explain: Auditors, reviewers, managers and developers can all check a cited answer.

questions.q: Analyst must explain model results. What helps most?
questions.explain: PRISM traces how a result is produced, step by step, with sources.
